title: 2D Environment setting: 2D Background image
content: ### Objective Add an image on 2D background. (Ver. MD7) ### Location 2D window Right click → Select Add/Edit Background Image on popup menu ### Operation **Adding image** Navigate to the menu indicated in Location. → Add/Edit Background Image menu will popup. Click on open image file and select an image want to add to background. → Move image ghost on 2D window to adjust position of the image. → After setting position and detail property, click OK to apply image to 2D window background. Scale | Adjust size of image by % ---|--- Rotation | Adjust rotation value of image Opacity | Adjust opacity of image Show Patterns | Adjust Show/Hide Patterns (ver. 12.1) ※ Note: A background image can be added onto the 2D window by dragging and dropping an image from the explorer window. (ver. 12.1) **Editing image** Navigate to the menu indicated in Location. → Readjust detail property and click OK. → Readjusted value will be applied. **Reset and delete image** Navigate to the menu indicated in Location. → Click Reset button on the bottom of the 2D Background dialog. → Back ground image will be deleted and detail property will be reset. → 2D Background image could be saved with 'Save as project'
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for adding, editing, and managing background images in a 2D window environment.

title: Select/Move/Transform Pattern
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Select Patterns to move, transform and rotate. #### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ### Operation #### Select 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern 2. Click the Pattern. → The Pattern is selected and highlighted in yellow. 3. To select multiple Patterns, hold down the Shift on the keyboard and click Patterns to be selected. → All clicked Patterns are now selected. 4. Or, click and drag on the 2D window to encompass all Patterns to be selected with a marquee box. → All Patterns inside the marquee box are selected. → The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) #### Move 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern 2. Click and drag the Pattern to be moved or use the arrow keys on keyboard. 3. Hold down the Shift key or Ctrl key (Mac: command) while moving the Pattern. → The Pattern can be moved in precise vertical, horizontal, or diagonal lines, or in its slope. 4. Or, right click or hit F1 key (Mac: Ctrl) while moving the Pattern to type in distance moved. #### Transform 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern 2. Select the Pattern to be transformed and click and drag desired point of the marquee box. → The selected Pattern is enlarged or shrunken. #### Rotate 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern 2. Select the Pattern to be rotated. 3. Select the Rotation Point, the single point above the marquee box, and drag left or right. → When the pivot point, the point at the center of the Pattern, is deactivated (in white,) the Pattern is rotated based on the center of the Pattern. ※ Note: To select point or segment, use the Edit Pattern tool or the Transform Point/Segment tool. Double click the pivot point to activate and transform or rotate based on the pivot point.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for selecting, moving, transforming, and rotating 2D patterns within the design software.

title: Apply Substance SBSAR Materials to Trims, Buttons, and Avatars
content: ### Objective Allows the user to apply high-quality Substance materials to assets other than cloth patterns within Marvelous Designer. ### Location Fabric ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Substance ### Operation 1. Load garment and avatar. 2. Add trim or button to garment. 3. Select the Fabric viewer in a window dropdown menu. 4. In the Property Editor for a selected fabric, set the Material to 'Substance'. → Click on the four-square button next to the Substance logo and import a Substance (.sbsar) file. 5. Click on any Trim, Button, or part of the Avatar. 6. Navigate to the Fabric window, select the Fabric the Substance material is assigned to, then select 'Assign' at the top of the Fabric window. → Observe that the Substance material has been applied to the Trim, Button, or Avatar component.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to apply high-quality Substance materials to various assets in Marvelous Designer, enhancing their garment designs.

title: Show 3D Grid
content: ### Objective Show or hide 3D grid. ### Location ### Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show 3D Grid Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ Environment ▶ Show 3D Grid → Show or hide 3D grid. ※ Note: It is also possible to show or hide 3D grid on the Marvelous Designer Viewer.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for toggling the visibility of the 3D grid in the application.

title: Avatar Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
content: ### Objective Set the Zipper or Slider via the right-click pop-up menu. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the avatar. → The pop-up menu appears. **Avatar Options** **Menu** | **Descriptions** ---|--- Select All Faces | Select and modify all surfaces of an Avatar. Delete Avatar | Select an avatar and delete it individually. Delete All Avatars | Delete the entire avatar. Delete Scene and Prop | Delete the selected Scene and Prop. (ver. 2024.0) Delete All Scene and Props | Delete the entire Scene and Prop. Move Avatar/ Move All Avatars & Garments | Move Avatar or all Avatars and garments to the center of the 3D window or the ground. Reset Joints | Reset joints of the Avatars. Change Heels (ver MD10) | Make Avatars' heels up or down. Deactivate/Activate Avatar | Deactivate or activate avatars as needed. When it is deactivated, the garments do not recognize while simulation. Hide Avatar | Show or hide individual avatar. Show/Hide All Avatars | Show or hide all avatars. Refresh Textures | Refresh the textures of the avatar. Export to USD Layer | Export as USD Layer.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on using the right-click pop-up menu to set the Zipper or Slider for avatars in the 3D Toolbar.

title: Morph Target with AVT Files
content: ### Objective Apply morph target function onto the AVT files to change the avatar Pose or shape. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Avatar ### Operation 1. Open an Avatar in the 3D window. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Avatar → The Add Avatar or Open Avatar window appears. 3. Select Load as Morph Target for the Load Type and select OK. → If morphing succeeds, the first avatar Pose or shape changes to the second avatar Pose or shape. → If morphing fails, a warning pop-up window appears and no change is made.
content_description: This web page provides guidelines for applying morph target functions to AVT files, enabling users to modify an avatar's pose or shape effectively.

title: Apply Normal Map To Graphic Image
content: ### Objective Apply Normal Maps to graphics for more realistic visualization. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic 2D Toolbar ▶ Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic 2D Toolbar ▶ Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic 2. Select a graphic image to apply Normal Map. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Material ▶ Texture ▶ Normal Map → The intensity value range of -10 to 10 can be applied automatically as entered. → The higher the value, the bumpier expression, the less the value, the less bumpier expression.
content_description: This webpage guides users on how to apply Normal Maps to graphics for enhanced realism in 2D visualizations.

title: Invert Selection
content: ### Objective Invert the Pattern selection, selecting the Patterns currently not selected. ### Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) ▶ Invert Selection Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Invert Selection ### Operation 1. Select Patterns that will be deselected. 2. Follow the indicated guideline as below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) ▶ Invert Selection Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Invert Selection → All Patterns that were selected are deselected, while the remaining patterns are selected.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for inverting the selection of patterns, allowing users to quickly deselect currently selected patterns and select those that were previously unselected.

title: Eyedropper
content: ### Objective Use Eyedropper tool to extract any desired colors not only from Marvelous Designer, but any other websites or images just by clicking the colors. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color ▶ Eyedropper ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Color ▶ Eyedropper 2. Move mouse cursor to desired area. → The mouse cursor icon is now being changed to an eyedropper-shaped. 3. Click on a desired area to extract a color. → The extracted color sample appears in the window. 4. To exit the tool, click on the Eyedropper icon again or press ESC on keyboard.
content_description: "Learn how to easily extract colors from any website or image using the Eyedropper tool in Marvelous Designer."

title: BUTTONHOLE STYLE PROPERTIES: Buttonhole Size
content: ### Objective Adjust buttonhole sizes as desired. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Size ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Buttonhole Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ Size 2. Type in the desired size value. → The buttonhole size is now being adjusted and applied.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for adjusting buttonhole sizes using the Property Editor in the Object Browser.

title: Delete Curve Point
content: ### Objective Delete unnecessary curve points when editing Patterns. When all curve points on a segment is deleted, it turns to a straight line. ### Location #### Delete Selected Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Curve Point #### Delete All Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) ▶ Delete All Curve Points ### Operation #### Delete Selected 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Edit Curve Point 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Curve Point 2. Right click on the curve point to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. Or, select the curve point and hit Delete key on the keyboard. ※ Note: * When you delete a segment point added on a curved line, all curved points on that specific line are deleted and so as the curvature. #### Delete All 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the 2.png Edit Pattern tool. Then, select a segment which all curved points should be deleted. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Segment) ▶ Delete All Curve Points → All curve points on the selected segment are deleted.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for deleting unnecessary curve points in 2D patterns to streamline editing and convert segments into straight lines.

title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Topstitch Style Preset
content: ### Objective Utilize the provided Topstitch presets to quickly visualize a variety of Topstitch styles. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Stitch ▶ Preset ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Stitch ▶ Preset 2. Based on the chart below, select the desired preset. → The selected Topstitch changes based on the choice. Custom | Use the Custom preset to input the desired values for the Topstitch style. ---|--- Bartack | ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438733864857) Buttonhole | ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438740492313) Single | ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438734363033) Overlock | ![Overlock.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438734636057) Pickstitch | ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438741304985) Zigzag | ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438741598873) ※ Note: * If any individual setting is changed after a provided preset is selected, the Preset automatically changes to Custom. * You can select either Texture or OBJ from the Type menu in the Property Editor. (Ver. 11)
content_description: This web page provides a quick guide to using Topstitch presets in the Property Editor to visualize and customize various Topstitch styles efficiently.

title: Animation Import
content: ### Objective Import Animation cache data created in the third-party 3D solutions. ※ Note: Refer to the links below for FBX/ Alembic file import:. * [3D File (FBX) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232885017) * [3D File (Alembic) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358253053081) ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Animation ▶ * Maya Cache(.mc) * Maya Cache(.mcx) * Point Cache 2 * MDD Cache(Standard) * MDD Cache(Maya/3ds Max) * Cache(Maya/3ds Max) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Animation ▶ ● Maya Cache (.mc) ● Maya Cache (.mcx) ● Point Cache 2 ● MDD Cache(Standard) ● MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max) → The File Explorer or Find window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click OK. → An option window appears with settings that apply to the file format selected. 3. Set the following individual settings. Object | Select All Avatars | Apply the cache data to all objects in the 3D environment. Cache data can be applied to individual objects from the submenu. ---|---|--- FPS | Set the frame rate of the cache data. ※ Note: This menu only appears when importing Point Cache (PC2) files. Scale | Set the scale of the cache data. Axis Conversion | Set the axis direction for the cache data. The Y-axis runs vertically by default. Garment Position | Move Avatar & Garment to Start Position | Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). Transition Animation | A transition animation is an animation that changes from a T-pose to a motion’s first pose in stages, and is created when the avatar’s current pose and motion differs from that of the first frame pose. 4. Click OK. → The cache data is imported according to the selected settings.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for importing animation cache data from third-party 3D solutions into your project, detailing the steps and settings required for various file formats.

title: Open/Save Bounding Volume
content: ### Objective Save newly created Bounding Volume, open and use previously saved Arrangement Points. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Open / Save ### Operation #### Open 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Open → Open File window appears. 2. Select the desired file and click Open to load. #### Save 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Arrangement ▶ Bounding Volume ▶ Save → Save File window appears. 2. Select the desired location to store. 3. Enter the desired file name and click Save. → A .pan file is now being created.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for saving new Bounding Volume files and accessing previously saved Arrangement Points in the Avatar Editor.

title: Rotate
content: ### Objective Rotate Patterns and Internal Shapes/Lines based on various references. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Rotate 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Select the Pattern or Internal Shapes/ Lines or Baselines to be rotated. → The marquee box appears around the selected item. 3. Click and drag the rotate point on top of the marquee box. → The selected item rotates towards the mouse. ※ Note: * While clicking and dragging the Pattern, Internal Shapes/Lines, or Baselines, right click to access the Rotate window. Type in the desired angle, then click OK. The selected item rotates based on the entered value (ver3.2.0). #### Clockwise/Counterclockwise 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select Clockwise (45º) or Clockwise (90º) or Counterclockwise (45º) or Counterclockwise (90º) → The selected pattern rotates according to the chosen options. #### X/Y Axis 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select X-Axis or Y-Axis. 4. Select the line of a Pattern which should be rotated to the chosen axis. → The selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to X-Axis or Y-Axis on the basis of the selected line. #### Parallel To 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Click on the Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines to be rotated. Then, right click to access the pop-up menu. 3. When the pop-up menu appears, select Parallel to... 4. Select the line of any Patterns or Internal Lines/Shapes in the 2D window which the previously selected Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines are rotated to. This line acts as a fiducial line. → The selected line turns red. 5. Then, select the line of the rotating Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines that will rotate parallel to the fiducial line selected above. → The Pattern or Internal Shapes/Lines rotates parallel to the fiducial line.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to rotate patterns and internal shapes/lines in a 2D design environment, utilizing various reference points and transformation options.

title: Windows - Marvelous Designer / Hardware Authentication Version Installation
content: ### Objective Install Windows - Hardware Authentication Version. Version: -Enterprise Network (Hardware Authentication) -Academic Perpetual (Hardware Authentication) ### Operation 1. Run the install file. In absence of an install file, download it from the '[http://marvelousdesigner.com](http://marvelousdesigner.com/) > Profile>LICENSE PURCHASE HISTORY'. 2. After running the install file, press "Next" on the setup window to continue installation. ![install_N_001.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438583386777) 3. Review the License Agreement and click "I Agree" to accept the terms of the agreement. ![install_N_002.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438627876505) ![install_N_003.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438628081305) 4. Choose a location to install the program. ![install_N_004.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438628213401) 5. Select a Start Menu folder. ![install_N_005.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438583978777) 6. The product begins installing. It takes less than a minute. ![install_N_006.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438628463769) 7. The Sentinel HASP Driver will also be installed so that the Dongle can be used. After the installation is completed, click "Finish" to close the window. ![install_N_007.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438628602137) 8. Once the program has finished installation, a Server must be set up. 9. Click the link below and check to see if the Sentinel Admin Control Center screen shows up, as it does on the picture below: [ ACC Page ](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)[![accpage.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438584578201) ](http://localhost:1947/)If the following screen does not appear, the HASP Driver must be reinstalled: [Manual Sentinel HASP Driver Installation](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358213387161)As shown below, click on the "Configuration" menu on left of the ACC Page. ![configuration.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438584743193) 10. Select "Access to Remote License Managers" as below image. ![accesstoremote.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438629141273) 11. Check the "Aggressive Search for Remote Licenses" item as shown below. Enter the IP address of the Server PC in the "Specify Search Parameters" item. Click the "Submit" button. 12. If the HASP Key can be seen as shown below after approximately 10 seconds, then the configuration is successful. ![sentinelkey.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438629372953) ※ Note: Identifying Server PC's IP Address Start (Windows) Button ▶ All Programs ▶ Accessories ▶ Command Prompt ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' or enter 'cmd' in the 'Run' menu ▶ Enter 'ipconfig' Reference site: <http://www.ghacks.net/2011/05/17/network-troubleshooting-basics-the-ipconfig-command/>
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for installing the Hardware Authentication version of Windows for both Enterprise Network and Academic Perpetual licenses.

title: Fold Pattern
content: ### Objective Use this function to create a pressing effect by adjusting the angle of Pattern's Internal Line, for instance, pressed lines of formal trousers, fold direction of pleats. ### Location Pattern Property Editor ▶ Fold ▶ Fold Angle ### Operation 1. Click on an Internal Line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pattern Property Editor ▶ Fold ▶ Fold Angle 3. Adjust the value of Fold Angle as desired. ※ Note: Fold Strength | Sets the angle closer as the value increases. The value range is in between 0 to 20. ---|--- Fold Angle | Sets the value in the range of 0˚ to 360˚, 180˚ represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0˚, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360˚. Fold Rendering | Sets whether the pleats to have soft or sharp edges according to user preference. (Only applicable if Fold Arrangement is used on an Internal line.)
content_description: This webpage provides a guide for adjusting the Fold Angle in Pattern's Internal Line to create realistic pressing effects for garments like formal trousers and pleats.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Physical Property Preset
content: ### ![Presets.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438811408409)Objective Some of the Physical Properties with detailed property values are adjusted beforehand as Presets for easier use. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Preset

content: ### Objective When you create Patterns in the 2D window, the last Pattern created is placed on the front by default. Change the order of the Patterns as needed. ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Order ▶ Bring Forward / Bring to Front / Send Backward / Send to Back ### Operation 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Patterntool. 2. Select the Pattern or Internal Line or Shape to be reordered. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Order ▶ Bring Forward / Bring to Front / Send Backward / Send to Back →The selected object is reordered.

title: MODULAR MODE: Edit Block Folders in the Modular Configurator Window
content: ### Objective Edit Block folders at your convenience to organize Blocks in the folders. ### Location Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator ▶ (Select) Block Folder ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Vertical Menu Tab on the Left ▶ Modular Configurator ▶ (Select) Block Folder → All Blocks in the selected Block folder appears in the Modular Configurator. 2\. Select the Edit button. → Show icons appear on every Garment thumbnails. 3\. Select a Modular Structure file that you want to organize first. → All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. 4\. Click on the Display icon to either display or hide the Garments or Blocks → Hidden Garments or Blocks appear in lighter shade and the displayed Garments or Blocks appear in brighter shade. 5\. Click on the Save button to save in the configuration file in the same folder as the Block. 6\. When editing is done, select the Exit button. → The Blocks appear in the Modular Configurator accordingly. ※ Note: * It is able to tie the Modular configuration files as a group by adding a group in the Editor Mode when needing a category that is above all the Modular configuration files. * Unlikely to the Blocks, one Modular configuration file can only be included in one group.
content_description: Organize and manage your Block folders efficiently using the Modular Configurator to enhance your workflow.

title: Avatar (*.avt) Add
content: ### Objective Use the Add Avatar function to load and work on several Avatars from the 3D Garment window in one go. This function can be used when loading and coordinating belt buckles, buttons, armor, and other hard objects. Furthermore, it can also be used when designing Garments that are connected to two avatars. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Avatar → The Open File window appears. 2. Select the Avatar to be added and click Open. → The Add Avatar window appears (ver2.4.0). 3. Select the appropriate settings and click OK to place the Avatar. ※ Note: * Add Avatar Options Placement | X | Move along the X axis (left, right) relative to the center of the 3D Window. ---|---|--- Y | Move along the Y axis (top, bottom) relative to the center of the 3D Window. Z | Move along the Z axis (front, back) relative to the center of the 3D Window. Unit | Set unit for placement. * As shown in the image below, the Add Avatar function can load and use human-shaped Avatars, as well as parts needed for production, such as helmets, shoulder pads, armor and petticoats. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438529090969) * When using multiple Avatars, save as Project file to save all Avatars (ver2.3.0).
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide on using the Add Avatar function to efficiently load and manage multiple avatars for 3D garment design, including coordinating accessories and hard objects.

title: Cache Animation Export
content: ### Objective Export Animation cache data. ※ Note: Only the cache data related to the Garment can be exported. ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation * Maya Cache (.mc) * Maya Cache (.mcx) * Point Cache 2 * MDD Cache (Standard) * MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max) Operation * Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation ● Maya Cache (.mc) ● Maya Cache (.mcx) ● Point Cache 2 ● MDD Cache(Standard) ● MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max) → The Save File window appears. * Select the desired file and click OK. → The Export window opens. Set the full details and click OK. Object | Single Object Exports the selected object as a single object. | Multiple Objects Exports the selected object as multiple objects. ---|---|--- UnWeld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version 2.3.0. (ver2.3.0). | Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns (ver2.3.0). Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of the object. Animation | Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.) | Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) File | * Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. * Save with Meta Data (.xml) : Export the garment's pattern (Mesh), physical property, and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). * Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save the garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). * Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude the Ambient color value when saving materials (ver2.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for exporting garment-related animation cache data from Maya, detailing the steps and options available for various file formats and settings.

title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement
content: ### Objective Take avatar's circumference measurements by measuring its surface curves. There are two options for circumference measurement. Basic Circumference measurement simply measures its circumference. Surface Measurement measures exactly following avatar's shape. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurements ▶ Basic Circumference Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Measurements ▶ Basic Circumference Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) ▶ Measurement Toolbar ▶ (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) ▶ Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement 2. Click on one end of desired circumference measurement. 3. Click on the other end. 4. Mouse over a spot between the two points to set the circumference measurement angle. → Temporary line appears in purple. 5. Click when the desired angle of the circumference line appears.
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for accurately measuring the circumference of an avatar using basic or surface measurement techniques.

title: Guide for Installing Network Offline Version on the Internet Environment
content: ### Guide for Installing Network Version on the Internet Environment ### Objective Set up Marvelous Designer/Marvelous Designer Network Version on the Internet environment. Note that you do not need to follow the set-up guidelines below when a Server PC and Client PC are under the same local network environment. Simply plugging the dongle key into a Server PC enables you to run Marvelous Designer or Marvelous Designer on any PCs under the same local network as the Server PC located without any extra settings. ### 1.) Set-up on Server PC ### Operation #### 1\. Plug the dongle key in the Server PC and install the HASP Driver. HASP Driver gets automatically installed during the software installation. However if any trouble occurs during the process or in case of Server only being connected with the dongle key, HASP Driver should be installed manually. #### [Guideline for Sentinel HASP Driver Manual Installation ](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585) 2\. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should be automatically opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. #### 3\. Make sure the local IP address of the Server is static. (Local IP is dynamically allocated Intranet IP by the router.) The local IP address gets changed when the router is restarted if the local IP is not set in static status. To avoid repetitive IP reset in the process, 'port forwarding', set your Server's local IP as 'static'. #### 4\. Port-forward Port 1947 for TCP and UDP of the Server's local IP in the router setting. Port-forwarding enables to transmit the data from Client/Server to Server/Client through Port 1947. Port-forwarding method vary considerably in the types of router therefore please ask for support from your network manager. ※ Note: [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_forwarding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_forwarding) [http://www.wikihow.com/Set-up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router](https://www.wikihow.com/Set-Up-Port-Forwarding-on-a-Router) ### ### 2.) Set-up on Client PC ### Operation 1\. Run Marvelous Designer/Marvelous Designer Network Version installer. 2\. Make sure Port 1947 is open in the firewall. Port 1947 should automatically be opened once the HASP Driver gets installed however, occasionally it fails to open the port in certain PCs. In this case, go to the firewall settings and open the port manually. Port 1947 is being used for communication between the Client PC and the dongle key in the Server PC in order to get an authentication. Setting methods varies considerably in the types of firewall, therefore please ask for support from your network manager. 3\. Set external IP of the Server on the dongle key configuration to let the software reaches the Server for an authentication. This can be done through Sentinel Admin Control Center which is automatically installed during the HASP Driver installation. Access to [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) Click on 'Configuration' (the red box) ![3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438789862425) 4\. Click on the third tab, which is called, 'Access to Remote License Managers'. ![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438790034457) 5\. Make sure to check on 'Aggressive Search for Remote License' and to type the Server PC's external IP in 'Specify Search Parameters' (note that the external IP is different from the local IP mentioned in the 'Set-up on Server PC'). You are able to see the external IP of the Server PC on the website ([http://www.whatismyip.com/](https://www.whatismyip.com/)). ![1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438796362137)
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for setting up the Marvelous Designer Network Version in an Internet environment, detailing the necessary steps for both Server and Client PCs to ensure proper installation and connectivity.
